title: Cheap Gifts, Good Taste: WIRED-Tested Picks Under $25
gist: A WIRED-tested gift guide of items under $25 (Field Notes, Muji pens, Ugreen trackers, Kiwi knives, etc.), framed by the observation that $25 buys far less than a decade ago as gas nears $5 a gallon and wages lag.

insights.claim: The author argues $25 no longer goes far: a decade ago it could fill a gas tank and buy a good gift, but now average national gas prices are inching toward $5 a gallon and wages have not kept up.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Anecdotal signal of consumer affordability strain heading into holiday season.
insights.quote: average national gas prices are inching toward $5 a gallon. And we all know wages have not kept up.

insights.claim: Ugreen FineTrack tracker tags work with Apple's Find My and perform indistinguishably from AirTags at about a quarter of the price ($24 for a four-pack).
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Low-cost Find My-compatible accessories erode Apple's tracker pricing power.
insights.quote: these Bluetooth trackers work just as well as AirTags for a quarter of the price

insights.claim: SmartLabels QR-code stickers use a free app with AI to catalog the contents of drawers and boxes so items can be located from a phone.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: AI features are trickling into cheap consumer organizing products.

insights.claim: WIRED's digital subscription is offered at $24 for the first year to new subscribers, rising to $48 a year after.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.locator: WIRED is the gift that keeps
